overview.title: Testing that protects your reputation and your roadmap.
overview.description: Production defects cost more than development time — they cost customer trust, support overhead, and engineering momentum. Yet many teams treat QA as a final gate rather than a continuous practice embedded in every sprint. Forgeone helps organizations build quality into their development process: automated regression suites, performance testing under realistic load, security validation, and manual exploratory testing for the edge cases automation misses. The result is software your team ships confidently and your users trust.

faqs.title: Common questions about QA and testing.

items.question: Should we automate all our testing?
items.answer: No — and teams that try often waste effort automating brittle UI tests while missing critical edge cases. We follow the testing pyramid: heavy unit and integration test automation, targeted end-to-end automation for critical paths, and manual exploratory testing for usability and edge cases.

items.question: Can you integrate with our existing CI/CD pipeline?
items.answer: Yes. We integrate automated tests into GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, or whatever pipeline you use. Tests run on every commit with clear pass/fail reporting and failure notifications.

items.question: How do you handle testing for applications already in production?
items.answer: We start by building regression suites around existing functionality — capturing current behavior before new changes introduce risk. This creates a safety net that enables confident iteration on live products.

items.question: Do you provide QA engineers or just automation?
items.answer: Both. We embed QA engineers who perform manual testing, exploratory validation, and test planning alongside automation developers who build and maintain test suites. The combination catches defects that either approach alone would miss.

items.question: How do you measure testing effectiveness?
items.answer: We track defect escape rate, test coverage by layer, mean time to detect defects, and release confidence scores. Quality metrics are shared with engineering and product stakeholders so testing impact is visible, not assumed.
